# Rule index: shared

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-rule-index.mjs from the rule docs. Do not edit; change the doc and regenerate. -->

Every rule ID of the shared docs (all stacks) with its headline, grouped by doc. The headline is the rule's first sentence; the full rule (details, values, examples, *Why*) is in the doc. **Before you implement against a rule, read its full text**: search the doc for the ID and read that bullet, or read the doc when the task is centred on its topic. MUST = deviation needs an ADR; SHOULD = default, deviate with a stated reason; no keyword = MUST unless it says *prefer*, *default* or *consider*.

## [Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters)](../04-solution-strategy/hexagonal-architecture.md)

- ARCH-DEP-01: Every source-code dependency MUST point inward, toward the domain.
- ARCH-DEP-02: Domain code MUST NOT depend on application, ports, adapters, configuration or infrastructure frameworks (ORM, web, messaging, DI container).
- ARCH-DEP-03: When the core needs something from the outside, it MUST define an outgoing port, which an adapter implements (Dependency Inversion).
- ARCH-DEP-04: Application code MUST NOT instantiate adapters. Wiring happens only in the composition root (DI container or hand-written).
- ARCH-DEP-05: Adapters MUST NOT depend on each other.
- ARCH-DEP-06: SHOULD: design the domain first.
- ARCH-DEP-07: Read "single responsibility" as "a single reason to change", not as "does one thing".

## [Implementing Adapters](../05-building-block-view/adapters.md)

- ARCH-ADP-01: Protocol details MUST NOT leak into the core.
- ARCH-ADP-02: Incoming adapters call incoming ports only, never application services or outgoing ports directly.
- ARCH-ADP-03: Slice incoming adapters narrowly.
- ARCH-ADP-04: Each handler owns its request/response models, kept private to its package where the language allows.
- ARCH-ADP-05: Translate errors centrally per adapter.
- ARCH-ADP-06: If the core must actively push to an incoming adapter (websocket, server-sent events), define an outgoing port that the adapter implements.
- ARCH-ADP-07: Port input and output models live in the core (`domain` or `ports/out`), never in the adapter.
- ARCH-ADP-08: Outgoing ports are narrow (Interface Segregation).
- ARCH-ADP-09: Slice outgoing adapters freely.
- ARCH-ADP-10: Bounded contexts don't share outgoing adapters.
- ARCH-ADP-12: Technology-specific models (ORM entities, API DTOs) stay inside their adapter, with the narrowest visibility possible.
- ARCH-ADP-13: SHOULD: choose the simplest technology that fits.
- ARCH-ADP-14: An outgoing adapter does what its port method promises and nothing more.

## [Code Organization](../05-building-block-view/code-organization.md)

- ARCH-ORG-01: Every class/module MUST live in exactly one of `domain`, `application`, `ports/in`, `ports/out`, `adapter/in/<tech>`, `adapter/out/<tech>`, the composition root, or a support location that a stack doc names.
- ARCH-ORG-02: Adapters MUST be grouped by technology (`rest`, `kafka`, `jpa`, `s3`, …) and direction (`in` / `out`).
- ARCH-ORG-03: Versioned external APIs MUST be placed in version sub-packages (`adapter/in/rest/v1`, `v2`).
- ARCH-ORG-04: `application` is sub-divided by functional cut (feature, use-case group or aggregate), not by technical role.
- ARCH-ORG-05: Business exceptions belong in `domain`.
- ARCH-ORG-06: Names MUST reveal use cases ("screaming architecture").
- ARCH-ORG-07: Hide what isn't an entry point.
- ARCH-ORG-08: A neutral composition root wires the application.
- ARCH-ORG-09: Bounded contexts in one application are separated like separate services.

## [Implementing Use Cases](../05-building-block-view/use-cases.md)

- ARCH-UC-01: One application service per use case.
- ARCH-UC-02: Each use case is reachable only through its incoming port (an interface/contract in `ports/in`).
- ARCH-UC-03: Keep queries separate from commands.
- ARCH-UC-04: Every use case has its own input model (`SendMoneyCommand`, `RegisterAccountCommand`).
- ARCH-UC-05: Input models validate themselves when constructed and are immutable.
- ARCH-UC-06: Prefer complete constructors (or the language's equivalent) over builders for input models.
- ARCH-UC-07: Output models are use-case specific and minimal.
- ARCH-UC-08: `null` is not a valid "not applicable" value in an input model.
- ARCH-UC-09: Use the question above to decide where a rule goes.
- ARCH-UC-10: Business errors are exceptions; a result type is only for an expected alternative outcome (default, decision D7).
- ARCH-UC-11: The use case owns the transaction.
- ARCH-UC-13: Every error belongs to one category of the table below, and every adapter handles a category the same way.
- ARCH-UC-14: Domain events are immutable types in `domain`, named in the past tense (`OrderPlaced`), raised by the aggregate or the use case, and handed to an outgoing port by the use case inside its transaction.
- ARCH-UC-15: The use case authorizes; the incoming adapter authenticates.
- ARCH-UC-16: A rule that depends on other rows or on concurrent requests is enforced atomically, never by check-then-write alone.
- ARCH-UC-17: A command that may act on someone else's data carries the owner separately from the caller.
- ARCH-UC-18: Logic shared by several use cases of one cut lives in package-private final helper classes that each service builds, not in a shared bean.
- ARCH-UC-19: A bulk import of structured data (CSV, spreadsheet) follows four defaults, deviation stated in an ADR.
- ARCH-UC-20: Production code reads the time only from an injected clock, and the business date comes from one function in the product's time zone.
- ARCH-UC-12 (default D2): Use a rich domain model for logic-heavy domains.

## [Container Images, Frontend Delivery and Runtime Contract](../07-deployment-view/container-runtime.md)

- REL-IMG-01: Every deployable ships as an OCI image built once per commit in the pipeline (REL-CD-01).
- REL-IMG-02: Cloud Native Buildpacks are the default build method.
- REL-IMG-03: Base and builder images stay current.
- REL-FE-01: The BFF image embeds and serves the frontend bundle.
- REL-FE-02: The bundle reaches the BFF image as a pipeline artifact, not through a cross-component build (REPO-LAY-04).
- REL-FE-03: The BFF serves the bundle with fixed rules:
- REL-FE-04: During a rolling deployment both releases' chunks can be loaded (REL-ZD-04).
- REL-FE-05: The frontend embedded in the BFF is part of the BFF's release.
- REL-FE-06: A BFF that should serve the bundle refuses to start without it.
- REL-RUN-01: Containers run without privileges:
- REL-RUN-02: The root filesystem is read-only.
- REL-RUN-03: Every container has resource bounds.
- REL-RUN-04: The platform's start-up budget covers the worst-case start.
- REL-RUN-05: The JVM heap is derived from the container's memory limit, as a percentage, never a fixed `-Xmx` chosen without the limit in view.
- REL-RUN-06: The platform's termination grace period is longer than the application's shutdown budget plus any pre-stop delay plus a margin (OBS-04, Spring:
- REL-RUN-07: Images carry OCI labels `org.opencontainers.image.source` (repository URL), `org.opencontainers.image.revision` (commit SHA) and `org.opencontainers.image.title`.
- REL-RUN-08: A feature that depends on what the image provides beyond the runtime (fonts, AWT, native libraries, locale data, CA certificates) is exercised against the real image.

## [Delivery and Release](../07-deployment-view/delivery-and-release.md)

- REL-BR-01: Trunk-based development.
- REL-BR-02: `main` is protected:
- REL-BR-03: Pull requests are squash-merged and the squash commit message follows Conventional Commits 1.0.0:
- REL-BR-04: Fixes for a released version are made on `main` first.
- REL-BR-05: Branch protection is checked configuration, and ownership is explicit.
- REL-VER-01: Every deployable is versioned `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and released by a tag in the REPO-CI-05 format (`backend/v1.4.0`).
- REL-VER-02: Libraries and other published packages follow SemVer 2.0.0 strictly, derived from the Conventional Commits since the last release.
- REL-VER-03: The version is set by the release tooling, never by hand.
- REL-VER-04: Each deployable keeps a `CHANGELOG.md` in its folder (unless the product chose release notes only, REL-VER-03), grouped by type (features, fixes, breaking changes).
- REL-VER-05: Every running deployable reports its release version and commit, so an incident report names exactly what ran.
- REL-CD-01: Build once, promote the same artifact.
- REL-CD-02: The standard stages are:
- REL-CD-03: The production deployment requires an explicit, recorded manual approval enforced by the delivery platform.
- REL-CD-04: A release is blocked by each of the following:
- REL-CD-05: Where the customer deploys, each release is delivered as a handover package instead of a deployment:
- REL-CD-06: Pipeline rules name capabilities; the product records its tools.
- REL-CD-07: The pipeline is fast enough for roll-forward, and there is only one (SHOULD for the numbers).
- REL-CD-08: A product without a pipeline yet (no SCM host or CI chosen, a local demo installation as deliverable) runs the gates locally and records the gap.
- REL-DB-01: Migrations run before the new version takes traffic, with a separate DDL role.
- REL-DB-02: Every migration is compatible with the previous release still running (expand/contract, REL-ZD-03;
- REL-DB-03: Several instances, or a retried job, may start the migration at once.
- REL-DB-04: A migration finishes within its time budget.
- REL-DB-05: A failed migration stops the rollout.
- REL-DB-06: Migrations are linted in the pull request for statements that break REL-DB-02 or lock busy tables:
- REL-ZD-01: Production runs at least two instances of every server-side deployable (backends, BFFs, Next.js apps) and deploys rolling (SHOULD), so one instance always serves.
- REL-ZD-02: An instance receives traffic only when ready and stops receiving it before it stops.
- REL-ZD-03: Version N works with version N-1 on every boundary for at least one release:
- REL-ZD-04: Browsers that loaded the previous release keep working during and after a rollout.
- REL-RB-01: Roll forward by default.
- REL-RB-02: Rolling back the application is always possible for one release:
- REL-RB-03: The schema is never rolled back.
- REL-RB-04: The rollback is rehearsed before the first production go-live and then at least once a year (SHOULD for the yearly repeat):
- REL-RB-05: The product's chapter 7 states RPO and RTO for each data store and who backs up and tests restores (usually the platform operator).
- REL-FF-01: A feature flag is read through an outgoing port (e.g. `FeatureFlags` in `ports.out`, frontend:
- REL-FF-02: Every flag is registered with name, type, owner, creation date and removal date in one place per component (an enum or a flags file).
- REL-FF-03: Both states of every flag are tested at the test type of the element that reads it (one test per state, not all combinations).
- REL-FF-04: A flag is never an access control.

## [Repository Layout](../07-deployment-view/repository-layout.md)

- REPO-LAY-01: A product's backend and the frontends built for it live in one repository (default D12), each in its own top-level component folder.
- REPO-LAY-02: Every new project and every project plan is checked against the decision guide before the repositories are created.
- REPO-LAY-03: One component per folder, named by its role:
- REPO-LAY-04: No build orchestrator across components.
- REPO-LAY-05: Repo-wide files live at the root, component files in the component.
- REPO-LAY-06: The baseline is synced into the repository root, never into a component folder (command and options:
- REPO-LAY-07: The root `.gitignore` also ignores tool output (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `coverage/`, `.env*.local`), next to the IDE block of TOOL-IDE-03;
- REPO-API-01: A frontend in the same repository generates its client directly from the backend's committed spec (`frontend/orval.config.ts` → `../backend/openapi/orders-v1.yaml`).
- REPO-API-02: One commit is not one deployment.
- REPO-TOOL-02: Git hooks, if used, are installed from the component that owns the tooling and work from the git root.
- REPO-TOOL-03: Agents run stack commands from the component folder.
- REPO-CI-01: The pipeline runs the jobs in this table.
- REPO-CI-02: Contract and shared files trigger every affected component.
- REPO-CI-03: The merge gate is one always-reported status.
- REPO-CI-04: The `e2e:smoke` tier runs against a backend built from the same commit (08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/typescript.md, NG-TEST-08):
- REPO-CI-05: Each release unit is versioned separately, with tags prefixed by its component folder (`backend/v1.4.0`, `backend-admin/v2.1.0`).

## [Avoiding N+1 Requests over REST](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/avoiding-n-plus-one.md)

- API-N1-01: Every proposal or change that loads data across a REST boundary MUST be checked for N+1 requests and waterfalls.
- API-N1-02: The proposer recommends one strategy from the catalogue with its tradeoffs; the developer decides per use case.
- API-N1-03: Default order of preference:
- API-N1-04: Frontend mitigations (S4, S5) live in the outgoing adapter, typically as a decorator implementing the same port.
- API-N1-05: Backend batch and view endpoints MUST NOT reintroduce N+1 in persistence.
- API-N1-08: A view that needs data of several aggregates behind different ports is assembled in the use case ring, with one set-based read per port.
- API-N1-09: A read loads only the range its result needs.
- API-N1-06: Assert with tests.
- API-N1-07: Unbounded lists are not allowed.

## [OpenAPI Contracts](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/openapi-contracts.md)

- API-CON-01: Every REST API consumed by one of our clients MUST be described by an OpenAPI 3.x spec.
- API-CON-02: The spec is generated from the backend code (code-first) and never edited by hand.
- API-CON-03: The generated spec is committed, one file per API major version (`openapi/<api>-v1.yaml`), and CI regenerates it and fails if the committed file differs.
- API-CON-04: CI checks for breaking changes against the target branch (e.g. with `oasdiff breaking`).
- API-CON-05: The spec is designed, not just emitted.
- API-CON-06: Every new or changed endpoint is checked for N+1 usage by its consumers (08-crosscutting-concepts/api/avoiding-n-plus-one.md).
- API-CON-12: Schema names are unique across the API.
- API-CON-13: One operation that accepts several request media types declares one content entry per media type; one that returns a file declares its media type with a binary schema.
- API-CON-14: No two paths differ only in the name of a path template, and the spec is linted.
- API-CON-07: Consumers MUST NOT hand-write low-level HTTP calls or DTO types for an API that has a spec.
- API-CON-08: The consumer pins the spec it was generated from.
- API-CON-09: Generated code lives inside the outgoing adapter for that API and never leaves it (ARCH-ADP-12).
- API-CON-10: Responses are validated at runtime where the language doesn't guarantee the shape (TypeScript:
- API-CON-11: Mocks for adapter tests and stubbed E2E tests are generated from the same spec, so tests fail when the contract moves.

## [REST Conventions (wire format)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/rest-conventions.md)

- API-REST-01: Decimals and money are JSON strings, never JSON numbers.
- API-REST-02: Date and time use ISO 8601 / RFC 3339.
- API-REST-03: Enums are strings in the spec, never ordinals.
- API-REST-04: Optional fields are omitted when empty; required fields are never `null`.
- API-REST-05: Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`.
- API-REST-06: Status codes follow one table.
- API-REST-07: Every business error has a stable `code` from the API's catalogue.
- API-REST-08: Every collection endpoint is bounded: paged, or limited by a documented hard upper bound that the query enforces (API-N1-07).
- API-REST-09: Sorting uses a repeatable `sort` parameter, `sort=<field>,<asc|desc>` (`sort=createdAt,desc&sort=id,asc`).
- API-REST-10: Filtering uses one query parameter per filterable field, named after the response field.
- API-REST-11: Updates to resources that users change concurrently use optimistic concurrency, and a successful update answers `200` with the resource or its new version, never a bare `204`.
- API-REST-15: `GET` and `HEAD` never create or change persistent state.
- API-REST-16: Every date, month and period input is validated at the incoming adapter against a documented plausible window, and ranges have a maximum span.
- API-REST-14: A state transition of a singleton resource MAY be an action sub-resource `POST …/<singleton>/<verb>`; everything else uses nouns.
- API-REST-12: An operation, parameter or field that will be removed is deprecated first.
- API-REST-13: Checks answer in a fixed order: 401, then request-shape errors that need no data (400 for malformed input, 428 for a missing `If-Match`), then 403/404 decided by the use case, then 409/412 from the current state.

## [Enforcing Architecture Boundaries](../08-crosscutting-concepts/architecture-enforcement/enforcing-boundaries.md)

- ARCH-ENF-01: Every project MUST have automated architecture tests from day one that check the dependency rule for the reference layout.
- ARCH-ENF-02: Architecture tests MUST fail if they match no classes/files.
- ARCH-ENF-03: Use the narrowest visibility the language offers for adapter internals and service implementations.
- ARCH-ENF-04: The architecture tests check ARCH-DEP-05 automatically, with one slice per adapter (direction and technology), so a new adapter is covered without editing the test.
- ARCH-ENF-05: Cyclic dependencies between packages/modules are forbidden, and the architecture tests check it.
- ARCH-ENF-06: Consider build-module splits once the architecture is stable.
- ARCH-ENF-07: Adding an inter-module dependency is a reviewed decision, never a quick fix for a compile error.

## [Configuration and Environments](../08-crosscutting-concepts/configuration/configuration.md)

- CFG-01: Only values that differ between deployments are configuration.
- CFG-02: One build artifact per component and commit is promoted through every environment (REL-CD-01).
- CFG-03: Environment-specific values are injected at deploy time by the platform, as environment variables or mounted files.
- CFG-04: Profiles and build modes describe how the code runs, not where.
- CFG-05: Secrets live in a secret manager and reach the component as mounted files or environment variables injected by the platform.
- CFG-06: Every secret is rotatable without a code change or rebuild, by updating the secret manager and restarting (rolling) the component.
- CFG-07: Configuration objects that hold secrets never print them.
- CFG-08: Configuration is typed and validated at startup.
- CFG-09: Configuration is read only at the edge.
- CFG-10: Every key is documented where it is defined (the typed configuration class or schema), with meaning, unit and default.
- CFG-12: Each deployable component keeps a machine-readable list of the keys a deployment sets:
- CFG-11: A frontend gets its per-environment configuration at runtime from its serving origin, never at build time.
- TEST-CFG-01: Each configuration type has a binding test:
- TEST-CFG-02: The deployed defaults start.
- TEST-CFG-03: Secret masking is asserted (CFG-07):
- TEST-CFG-04: The key list matches the code.
- TEST-CFG-05: A required key has no deployed default.

## [Data Protection (GDPR / DSGVO)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/data-protection/data-protection.md)

- DP-INV-01: Every product keeps a personal-data inventory in `docs/data-protection/processing-record.md`, structured like an Art.
- DP-INV-02: Every product keeps a deletion concept in `docs/data-protection/deletion-concept.md`:
- DP-INV-03: A change that adds a personal-data field, a storage location, a purpose or a recipient updates both documents in the same pull request (like DOC-ARC-06) and is flagged for DPO review in the pull request.
- DP-INV-04 (SHOULD): A test checks that every table of the migrated schema is named in the deletion concept or on its list of tables without personal data.
- DP-MIN-01: Every personal-data field has a purpose in the inventory.
- DP-MIN-02: Personal data stays where it is needed.
- DP-MIN-03: Privacy-friendly defaults (Art. 25(2)):
- DP-MIN-04 (SHOULD): Views for roles that may see only aggregates never show a group smaller than the product's minimum group size (default 5 people).
- DP-RET-01: Every data category has a retention period and a start event (e.g. "contract end + statutory period", "last login + 24 months") from the deletion concept, decided by the controller.
- DP-RET-02: Deletion after the period is automated by a scheduled job per data category that calls a use case (e.g. `PurgeExpiredCustomerAccounts`) and is covered by tests (DP-TEST-01).
- DP-RET-03: Data under statutory retention is restricted, not deleted (Art. 17(3)(b), Art. 18):
- DP-RET-04: Immutable or long-lived stores hold no personal data in clear text.
- DP-RET-05: Backups are not edited for erasure; they expire.
- DP-DSR-01: Data subject rights are use cases, behind incoming ports, authorized for a dedicated role (or the user for self-service), audited (SPRING-SEC-22, NEST-SEC-33) and tested like any use case:
- DP-DSR-02: Each module that stores personal data contributes to export and erasure through its own port, so a new storage location cannot be forgotten:
- DP-DSR-03: Requests are answered within one month (Art. 12(3); extendable by two months with notice).
- DP-DSR-04: Identity verification of the requester is part of the business process, not something the export endpoint assumes.
- DP-DSR-05: An access or portability export contains all stored personal data of the requester, and nothing about other people.
- DP-ENV-01: Production personal data never enters non-production environments, local machines, CI, test fixtures, tickets, chat or prompts to AI tools (like SEC-INC-01 for secrets).
- DP-ENV-02: Pseudonymised production copies are personal data and fall under DP-ENV-01.
- DP-ENV-03: Debugging production issues uses production tooling with logged, role-based access, not data exports.
- DP-ENV-04: Demo data of a running installation is loaded by an incoming adapter that calls the use cases, active only under the `demo` profile (CFG-04).
- DP-PROC-01: Every external service that receives personal data is listed in the inventory before it goes live:
- DP-PROC-02: Transfers outside the EU/EEA need a documented basis (adequacy decision under Art.
- DP-PROC-03: The browser loads no third-party resources that transmit user data without need.
- DP-TEL-01: Logs, metrics, traces and frontend error reports contain no personal data beyond pseudonymous identifiers (SPRING-LOG-08, NEST-LOG-09).
- DP-TEL-02: Personal data is never part of a URL path or query string (`/customers?email=…`).
- DP-TEL-03: Telemetry stores have a retention period in the deletion concept, and session replay or user-level analytics are off unless the inventory names them and consent exists.
- DP-INC-01: A personal-data breach follows the incident runbook (SEC-INC-02) and its clock depends on our role.
- DP-REV-01: A pull request that touches personal data answers the "Personal data" row of the PR template's security section (SEC-REV-01; rules per area in security-review.md).
- DP-TEST-01: Deletion and data subject use cases are tested end to end through their adapters:
- DP-TEST-02: Tests assert the absence of personal data where it must not appear:

## [Agent Skills](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/agent-skills.md)

- TOOL-SKL-01: Docs win over skills.
- TOOL-SKL-02: Third-party skills are installed only through the `skills` CLI, pinned in `skills-lock.json`, and committed (`.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, lock file).
- TOOL-SKL-03: Every new skill and every update is reviewed like a dependency.
- TOOL-SKL-04: Installed third-party skills are never edited in place.
- TOOL-SKL-05: A skill whose core contradicts our architecture is not installed.
- TOOL-SKL-06: Own skills cite rule IDs instead of restating rules.
- TOOL-SKL-07: Skills are updated deliberately in the baseline repository, at least before each consuming project syncs the baseline:
- TOOL-SKL-08: Scripts and hooks shipped by the baseline or by own skills run on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- TOOL-SKL-09: A product loads only the skills and stack docs of its declared stacks (declared stacks).
- TOOL-SKL-10: Agents read the docs in steps and never load every doc of a stack at once.
- TOOL-SKL-11: The rule index is generated, never edited by hand.
- TOOL-SKL-12: Every rule starts with a bold headline that states the rule on its own as one sentence:
- TOOL-SKL-13: Agent checklists and sources live outside the rule docs.
- TOOL-SKL-14: Agents edit code with the editor tools, or run the formatter before a scripted multi-line replacement.
- TOOL-SKL-15: On a red gate, agents run the autofix commands first and hand-fix only what remains; they never loosen a rule to get green.

## [Architecture Documentation (arc42)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/architecture-documentation.md)

- DOC-ARC-01: Every product has an arc42 documentation in `docs/architecture/`, one Markdown file per chapter (`01-introduction-and-goals.md` … `12-glossary.md`), created from the template.
- DOC-ARC-02: Product chapters link to the baseline instead of repeating it.
- DOC-ARC-03: Decisions are ADRs in `docs/adr/` (D6), copied from `docs/adr/0000-template.md`.
- DOC-ARC-04: Chapter 11 lists the conscious shortcuts (their ADRs, ARCH-SC-02) and known technical debt with the trigger that would make the team pay it back.
- DOC-ARC-05: Diagrams are text in the Markdown file (Mermaid; PlantUML only if Mermaid cannot express it).
- DOC-ARC-06: The documentation changes in the same pull request as the architecture.
- DOC-ARC-07: Lean beats complete (SHOULD).
- DOC-ARC-08: The baseline follows the same structure.
- DOC-ARC-09: The baseline repository keeps `ARCHITECTURE.md` at its root current.
- DOC-ARC-10: Product business rules live in chapter 8, section "Business rules"; open assumptions in `docs/architecture/open-questions.md`.
- DOC-ARC-11: Product docs state only what exists; anything not built yet is marked as planned.

## [IDE Setup: VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/ide-setup.md)

- TOOL-IDE-01: The project's config files are the source of truth (`.editorconfig`, Prettier, ESLint, Java formatter).
- TOOL-IDE-02: Format on save and lint-fix on save are on in both IDEs wherever the project's formatter has an IDE integration.
- TOOL-IDE-03: Shared IDE settings are committed; personal ones are not.
- TOOL-IDE-04: Recommended extensions/plugins follow the stack, detected from the project (Angular, React and Next.js, NestJS, Vitest, Playwright, Java/Spring, OpenAPI, Docker).
- TOOL-IDE-05: Use the workspace TypeScript version (`node_modules/typescript` of the frontend component) in both IDEs, so editor errors match the build.
- TOOL-IDE-06: Settings IntelliJ only stores per user (e.g. "Reformat code" for Java under Actions on Save) are listed in the project README as a one-time step;
- TOOL-IDE-07: In a product repository with component folders (D12), the IDE opens the repository root and the shared settings live there.

## [File Exports and Generated Documents](../08-crosscutting-concepts/exports/file-exports.md)

- EXP-01: Every export is either for people or for a machine, and the product's docs say which.
- EXP-02: A machine format is written down and pinned by a test.
- EXP-03: A CSV meant to be opened in Excel is UTF-8 with a byte order mark; spreadsheets for people are preferably `.xlsx`.
- EXP-04: Export cells that start with a formula character are neutralised.
- EXP-05: XML, FO, SVG and HTML are built with a writer or a templating engine that escapes by context, never by string concatenation, even with manual escaping.
- EXP-06: Server-side rendering of HTML or SVG to PDF or images has no network access.
- EXP-07: Exports are produced by an outgoing file adapter behind a port and delivered as a binary download.
- EXP-08: Generated documents need no fonts, AWT or native libraries from the image.
- EXP-09: PDFs for people meet PDF/UA-1 and are checked automatically, plus once per release by hand.
- EXP-10: A heavy export loads its data inside the read transaction and renders outside it, behind a concurrency limit.

## [Internationalization (i18n)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/i18n/i18n.md)

- I18N-01: i18n is a project decision recorded as an ADR:
- I18N-02: Domain, ports and use cases contain no UI text.
- I18N-03: The API contract stays language-neutral.
- I18N-04: Locale tags are BCP 47 (`de`, `de-CH`, `en-GB`).
- I18N-05: The source locale is the only hand-written catalog;
- I18N-06: The user's language is a user setting.
- I18N-07: No string concatenation, no plural logic in code, no word-order assumptions.
- I18N-08: Every key has translator context:
- I18N-09: Fallback chain `user locale` → `language only` (`de-CH` → `de`) → source locale.
- TOOL-I18N-01: Weblate (self-hosted) is the translation tool unless the product ADR chooses another that meets the same constraint (self-hosted open source, no fees).
- TOOL-I18N-02: Translations flow through Git.
- TOOL-I18N-03: CI fails on any of these catalog errors:
- TOOL-I18N-04: A pseudo-locale (accented, expanded, bracketed text) is generated from the source catalog and used in development and tests only.
- TOOL-I18N-05: Release rule.
- TOOL-I18N-06: Machine translation is a draft source only.
- TOOL-I18N-07: Translator context is kept in a sidecar `context.json` next to each catalog and pushed to Weblate by CI (descriptions, max lengths, screenshot names).
- TOOL-I18N-08: Until the translation tool is connected, non-source catalogs are written in the repository, with context, and every string written by an agent or machine translation is marked for human review.
- TEST-I18N-01: Component tests render with the real source-locale catalog so role-and-name queries stay readable (TS-TEST-07);
- TEST-I18N-02: Playwright has locale projects:
- TEST-I18N-03: axe (TS-TEST-12) runs per locale project and asserts `html[lang]` and `dir` after a switch (WCAG 3.1.1):
- TEST-I18N-04: An overflow check runs on the main screens in the pseudo-locale:
- TEST-I18N-05: Backend contract tests send `Accept-Language` for each supported locale and for an unsupported one and assert that `code` is identical while `title`, `detail` and `Content-Language` match the locale (SPRING-REST-13, NEST-REST-21).
- TEST-I18N-06: A bundle parity test compares the key sets and `{n}` placeholders of all backend message bundles (Spring: `messages_*.properties`; NestJS: ICU JSON catalogs, NEST-I18N-02).
- TEST-I18N-07: Locale-sensitive formatting has unit tests in at least two locales (decimal and grouping separators, date order, currency position).
- TEST-I18N-08: A language switch re-formats what is already on screen.

## [Mapping Between Boundaries](../08-crosscutting-concepts/mapping/mapping-between-boundaries.md)

- ARCH-MAP-01: State-changing use case, incoming adapter → application: use full mapping (dedicated command per use case).
- ARCH-MAP-02: State-changing use case, application ↔ persistence: start with no mapping.
- ARCH-MAP-03: Queries: start with no mapping across all boundaries.
- ARCH-MAP-04: Mixing strategies in one codebase is expected, not untidy.
- ARCH-MAP-05: Revisit the strategy when a use case grows.
- ARCH-MAP-06: The team keeps these guidelines visible and revises them together.
- ARCH-MAP-07: The outer ring maps.
- ARCH-MAP-08: Mapping code is explicit and tested.

## [Messaging and Event Contracts](../08-crosscutting-concepts/messaging/messaging.md)

- MSG-EVT-01: Messages are either events or commands, and their names say which.
- MSG-EVT-02: Events describe business facts, not table changes.
- MSG-EVT-03: Payloads carry only what consumers need.
- MSG-EVT-04: Topic names follow `<context>.<stream>.v<major>` (`orders.order-events.v1`), in kebab-case per segment.
- MSG-ENV-01: Every message carries the same metadata:
- MSG-ENV-02: Payload data types follow the REST conventions:
- MSG-CON-01: Every topic a service produces SHOULD be documented in an AsyncAPI 3 document committed with the producer (`asyncapi/<context>-v<N>.yaml`), generated from code like the OpenAPI spec (D8) and checked in CI for staleness.
- MSG-CON-02: Within a major version, changes are additive only (the event equivalent of API-CON-04).
- MSG-CON-03: Consumers are tolerant readers.
- MSG-CON-04: A breaking change gets a new type version and a new topic (`orders.order-events.v2`).
- MSG-CON-05: Compatibility is tested with committed examples.
- MSG-ORD-01: Order is guaranteed only per key.
- MSG-ORD-02: Events carry the aggregate's version (or a sequence number) when consumers keep state from them, and the consumer ignores an event older than what it already applied.
- MSG-ORD-03: The number of ordering units of a topic (Kafka: partitions) is chosen up front and not increased casually:
- MSG-PUB-01: A message that must be consistent with a database change is never sent directly from the use case.
- MSG-PUB-02: The default pattern is a transactional outbox with a relay:
- MSG-PUB-03: Producers wait for a durable publish acknowledgement from the broker (Kafka: `acks=all`, all in-sync replicas) and use the broker's protection against duplicates from producer retries (Kafka:
- MSG-PUB-04: The outbox relay is observable and does not let one bad row block everything.
- MSG-IDM-01: Every consumer is idempotent.
- MSG-IDM-02: Deduplication uses the message `id` or natural idempotency.
- MSG-IDM-03: Idempotency is tested by delivering the same message twice and asserting one effect.
- MSG-ERR-01: Consumers classify failures by the error categories of ARCH-UC-13.
- MSG-ERR-02: Retries for a consumer are bounded, with exponential backoff and jitter (RES-RTY-03), and happen in the consumer's error handler (one retry layer:
- MSG-ERR-03: A poison message never blocks a partition.
- MSG-DLT-01: Dead-letter topics belong to the consuming service.
- MSG-DLT-02: Every dead letter raises an alert to the owning team and is logged once.
- MSG-DLT-03: Replay is a documented, tested procedure.

## [Observability and Operability](../08-crosscutting-concepts/observability/observability.md)

- OBS-01: Every deployed component exposes a liveness and a readiness endpoint that the platform probes.
- OBS-02: Liveness checks only the process itself.
- OBS-03: Readiness reports whether this instance can serve traffic:
- OBS-04: Shutdown is graceful.
- OBS-19: Probes exercise the serving connector.
- OBS-05: Probe and lifecycle behaviour is tested:
- OBS-06: Technical metrics come from the framework instrumentation.
- OBS-07: Business metrics are explicit and few:
- OBS-08: Metric tags have low, bounded cardinality.
- OBS-09: Metrics and traces are emitted by adapters and the application ring through an observation abstraction or an outgoing port, never by `domain` or `ports` (ARCH-DEP).
- OBS-10: Trace context propagates with W3C Trace Context (`traceparent`, `tracestate`) from the first server hop onwards:
- OBS-11: The trace id is the correlation id.
- OBS-12: Trace context from outside the trust boundary is not trusted.
- OBS-13: Sampling is set explicitly per environment as configuration (CFG-03), never left to a default nobody chose.
- OBS-14: Frontends report unhandled errors and failed backend calls through one global handler to an error-reporting tool.
- OBS-15: Source maps are uploaded privately to the error-reporting tool by CI and never served publicly (TS-SEC-05).
- OBS-16: The product team defines SLOs for its user-facing journeys and records them as quality scenarios in its chapter 10, with the SLI, target, window and owner.
- OBS-17: Every component has the minimal dashboard (table below) before its first production release.
- OBS-18: Alerts page on symptoms, not causes:

## [Resilience and Idempotency](../08-crosscutting-concepts/resilience/resilience.md)

- RES-TMO-01: Every outbound call MUST have an explicit connect timeout and an explicit read (response) timeout.
- RES-TMO-02: Timeouts are chosen from the caller's budget, not the callee's worst case.
- RES-TMO-03: Each client adapter has a test that proves the read timeout fires.
- RES-TMO-04: Timeouts form a ladder, from the outside in: gateway timeout > request budget > transaction timeout > statement timeout.
- RES-TX-01: No remote call (HTTP, messaging send, object storage, mail) runs inside an open database transaction.
- RES-TX-02: Transactions have a timeout, below the request budget (RES-TMO-04).
- RES-RTY-01: Only idempotent operations are retried automatically.
- RES-RTY-02: Retries are only for transient failures:
- RES-RTY-03: Retries use exponential backoff with jitter and a budget:
- RES-RTY-04: Retry in one layer only.
- RES-RTY-05: Retries are tested:
- RES-CAP-01: Concurrency towards each dependency is bounded (bulkhead).
- RES-CAP-02: The database connection pool is sized deliberately.
- RES-CAP-03: A circuit breaker SHOULD be added where a failing dependency is called often enough that fast failure matters.
- RES-CAP-04: Fallbacks never fake success.
- RES-IDM-01: Every state-changing entry point states whether it is idempotent, and how.
- RES-IDM-02: `POST` endpoints that clients may retry (payments, orders, anything a user can double-submit, any call from another service) accept an `Idempotency-Key` header.
- RES-IDM-03: The key is stored in the same transaction as the business change, with a unique constraint on (caller, key), as the first write of that transaction.
- RES-IDM-04: Keys have a time to live (default 24 hours, at least the client's longest retry window), and a scheduled job purges expired keys (RES-JOB-01).
- RES-IDM-05: Idempotency is tested at the use case and at the store.
- RES-IDM-06: Remote side effects are covered by the same idempotency.
- RES-JOB-01: A scheduled job is an incoming adapter that calls an incoming port (ARCH-ADP-02), like a controller.
- RES-JOB-02: In a deployment with more than one instance, every scheduled job either runs under a cluster-wide lock or is proven safe to run concurrently on all instances.
- RES-JOB-03: Jobs work in bounded batches and are safe to stop at any point:
- RES-JOB-04: A request that needs one remote call per item of a bulk input commits first and hands the calls to a job.
- RES-JOB-05: A scheduled job that must act once per business fact claims the fact with a primary-key insert before acting.
- RES-CCH-01: A cache is an adapter concern.
- RES-CCH-02: What may be cached:
- RES-CCH-03: Every cache has a maximum size and a time to live, and its invalidation is written down:
- RES-CCH-04: Local in-memory caches are the default.
- RES-CCH-05: Cached adapters are tested for a hit (the dependency is called once for two reads), expiry or eviction, and key separation per caller or tenant where RES-CCH-02 requires it.

## [Secure Pipeline](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/secure-pipeline.md)

- SEC-CI-01: CI runs the dependency scan, the secret scan and SAST on every pull request; findings at or above the gate's threshold in the table fail the build.
- SEC-CI-02: The pipeline itself is hardened.
- SEC-CI-03: Releases publish an SBOM (CycloneDX; backend JAVA-TOOL-17, frontend TS-TOOL-16) and signed build provenance stored with the artifact; target SLSA Build L2.
- SEC-CI-04: A passive DAST baseline scan runs nightly against a stack built from the same commit (REPO-CI-04).
- SEC-CI-06: Container images are scanned at three points:
- SEC-CI-07: Before a deployment the digest's provenance and signature are verified by the delivery platform (admission policy) or by a pipeline step;
- SEC-CI-08: One scheduled job checks the security dates:
- SEC-CI-09: A new dependency that parses untrusted input (files, archives, markup, documents), or that is large or young, gets a written dependency review before it is added.

## [Security Requirements and Threat Modelling](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/security-requirements.md)

- SEC-REQ-01: Every project states its ASVS 5.0 target level and its data classification in `docs/security/requirements.md`.
- SEC-REQ-02: Requirements of the target level that are not met are tracked as issues, with an owner.
- SEC-REQ-03: Reviews and threat models cite the ASVS 5.0 chapter, and the requirement ID where one matches, next to our rule IDs (SEC-REV-03).
- SEC-REQ-04: A penetration test by people outside the team runs before the first go-live, then at least yearly and after every major change.
- SEC-REQ-05: Each product records in `docs/security/requirements.md` whether the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) applies to it, decided with legal.
- SEC-CRY-01: TLS 1.2 is the minimum and TLS 1.3 the preference on every connection outside the developer machine:
- SEC-CRY-02: Passwords are stored only where the product cannot leave them to the IdP (SPRING-SEC-03, NEST-SEC-03), and then hashed with Argon2id (OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet parameters).
- SEC-CRY-03: Data at rest is encrypted according to its class (SEC-REQ-01).
- SEC-CRY-04: Keys live in a key management service or the secret manager, never next to the data they protect and never in git or images (SEC-INC-01).
- SEC-CRY-05: Security-relevant random values (tokens, ids that must not be guessed, nonces, salts) come from a cryptographically secure generator:
- SEC-CRY-06: The IdP's password and recovery policy has baseline defaults (ASVS 5.0 V6, NIST SP 800-63B), recorded in chapter 8 as IdP configuration.
- SEC-TM-01: A system-level threat model is kept in `docs/security/threat-model.md`:
- SEC-TM-02: A feature that adds an external entry point, an outbound call, a role, or personal data gets a short threat model in its pull request, answering four questions:
- SEC-TM-03: Abuse cases are written next to the use cases and become tests.

## [Security Review](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/security-review.md)

- SEC-REV-01: A pull request that touches authentication, authorization, input handling, outbound calls, deserialization, file handling, headers, security configuration or personal data answers the security section of the PR template in its description.
- SEC-REV-02: Never weaken, skip, delete or make advisory a check to make a build pass.
- SEC-REV-03: Reviews cite the rule ID and the matching ASVS 5.0 chapter or requirement, or the Top 10:2025 category, for example "SPRING-SEC-16, ASVS V8, A01".

## [Vulnerability Management, Secrets, Audit Trail and Incidents](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/vulnerability-management.md)

- SEC-VUL-01: Every finding is triaged: dependency, SAST, secret and image scans (including the scheduled re-scan, SEC-CI-06), DAST, penetration tests (SEC-REQ-04), and reports from outside (`SECURITY.md`).
- SEC-VUL-02: Fix times by severity: critical 7 days, high 30, medium 90, low best effort, counted from detection or report, not from triage.
- SEC-VUL-03: An accepted risk is recorded in `docs/security/exceptions.md` with owner, reason and an expiry date, approved by the tech lead.
- SEC-INC-01: Secrets never enter git, logs, container images, tickets or chat.
- SEC-INC-02: Each project has a `SECURITY.md` (how to report a vulnerability) and a short incident runbook in `docs/security/incident-runbook.md`:
- SEC-INC-03: Secret scanning runs before the secret can spread:
- SEC-AUD-01: Security events (SPRING-SEC-22, NEST-SEC-33) go to an audit trail that the application cannot change or delete:
- SEC-AUD-02: The audit trail identifies people by pseudonymous ids only and has its own retention period in the deletion concept (DP-INV-02), decided by the controller with the DPO.
- SEC-AUD-03: Spikes of denied access and token validation failures raise an alert.
- SEC-AUD-04: Expired audit events are removed by a separate privileged path, never by the application role.
- SEC-AUD-05: A bulk export of personal data writes an audit event.

## [Test-Driven Development](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/tdd.md)

- TEST-TDD-01: Production code is written to make a failing test pass.
- TEST-TDD-02: Red first, and for the right reason.
- TEST-TDD-03: Green with the simplest code that passes.
- TEST-TDD-04: Refactor is part of every cycle, with all tests green: remove duplication, improve names, and also clean up the tests.
- TEST-TDD-05: One behavior per cycle, in vertical slices.
- TEST-TDD-06: For features on a main user path, use the double loop.
- TEST-TDD-07: London style mocks only contracts we own:
- TEST-TDD-08: Don't mock what you don't own.
- TEST-TDD-09: Mock commands, stub queries.
- TEST-TDD-10: Switch to Chicago when a double would duplicate the implementation:
- TEST-TDD-11: Expected values come from an independent source of truth:
- TEST-TDD-12: Test names state behavior in domain language ("rejects a transfer that would overdraw the account"), not method names.
- TEST-TDD-13: Every bug fix starts with a failing regression test that reproduces the bug (TEST-ARCH-11).
- TEST-TDD-16: Test data is explicit and deterministic.
- TEST-TDD-17: Fake-data libraries SHOULD be used only for volume and realism, not for the values a test asserts on.
- TEST-TDD-14: Agents work in visible cycles.
- TEST-TDD-15: Agents pick the style from the element table and say so when it deviates (e.g. "Chicago here, because the mapper is a pure function").

## [Testing by Architecture Element](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/testing-by-architecture-element.md)

- TEST-ARCH-01: Domain entities → unit tests.
- TEST-ARCH-02: Use cases (application services) → unit tests with mocked/faked outgoing ports.
- TEST-ARCH-03: Incoming adapters → integration tests inside the real framework (routing, serialization, validation, error mapping), with the incoming port mocked.
- TEST-ARCH-04: Outgoing adapters → integration tests against the real technology.
- TEST-ARCH-13: Every new value of a persisted enum, and every new kind of row in an existing table, is exercised once through the real adapter and the real migrations.
- TEST-ARCH-05: Main user paths → system tests.
- TEST-ARCH-06: Tests are written while implementing, not afterwards.
- TEST-ARCH-07: Narrow ports make mocking easy.
- TEST-ARCH-08: Tests must not break on pure refactorings.
- TEST-ARCH-09: Line coverage is not the success metric.
- TEST-ARCH-10: The measure is confidence to ship.
- TEST-ARCH-11: For every production bug, answer "Why didn't our tests catch this?", record the answer (e.g. in the bug ticket), and add a test that would have caught it.
- TEST-ARCH-12: Mutation testing on `domain` and `application` is optional (consider it as a test-strength signal).

## [UI Patterns: Responsive Layout, Screen Readers and Screen States](../08-crosscutting-concepts/ui/ui-patterns.md)

- UI-01: Layouts adapt to the Material Design window size classes:
- UI-02: Navigation follows the window size:
- UI-03: Spacing follows the 4/8 px grid, through a small set of spacing custom properties defined once next to the theme.
- UI-22: Navigation between routes is a `nav` landmark with links, and the current one has `aria-current="page"`.
- UI-04: Window size is UI-adapter state.
- UI-05: Data loading doesn't depend on the size class.
- UI-06: CSS first, code when the component tree changes.
- UI-07: Shells and pages respond to the window; reusable `shared/ui` components respond to their container (`container-type: inline-size`, `@container` queries).
- UI-08: Every new screen states its layout for compact, medium and expanded (canonical layout, navigation form, what moves where) in its spec or story;
- UI-09: Layout CSS uses logical properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-block`, `inset-inline`, `text-align: start`) and `rem`, not physical left/right or px font sizes.
- UI-10: Wide content never forces page-level horizontal scrolling.
- UI-11: Full-height and fixed elements use dynamic viewport units and safe areas:
- UI-12: Hover is an enhancement.
- UI-13: Form inputs set `type`, `autocomplete` and `inputmode`, and fields are full width on compact.
- UI-14: Print is out of scope by default.
- UI-15: Status messages (A11Y-20) use a visible `role="status"` region or the form field's error element where possible; otherwise the app announcer.
- UI-16: Route title and focus (A11Y-21):
- UI-17: Snackbars and toasts are polite, short, and never the only place for an error or a required action;
- UI-18: Dialogs are labelled by their visible title, focus moves into the dialog and returns to the trigger on close;
- UI-19: Loading, empty and error states use shared components from `src/shared/ui`:
- UI-20: A command cannot be submitted twice while it runs.
- UI-21: A dialog or panel with entered data does not discard it on Escape or a click outside.

## [Accessibility: WCAG 2.2](../10-quality-requirements/accessibility.md)

- A11Y-01: Every UI MUST conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
- A11Y-02: Every UI SHOULD meet the adopted AAA set above.
- A11Y-03: Conformance is asserted by automated tests in CI. An AA violation fails the build.
- A11Y-04: Accessibility tests and rules MUST NOT be disabled or weakened to make a build pass (SEC-REV-02).
- A11Y-26: Each product records whether accessibility law applies to it, decided together with legal and stated in its `docs/accessibility.md`:
- A11Y-27: Each product keeps a journey and screen inventory in its `docs/accessibility.md`: per main journey its routes, its states (dialog open, error shown, empty result, loading) and an owner.
- A11Y-05: Every UI project has all of these layers:
- A11Y-06: A green automated run is not conformance.
- A11Y-07: Native semantics first.
- A11Y-08: Design-system components before custom widgets.
- A11Y-09: Design tokens meet contrast in every theme (light, dark, high contrast):
- A11Y-10: Pointer targets are at least 24 × 24 CSS px (AA 2.5.8); 44 × 44 is the default (AAA 2.5.5).
- A11Y-11: The WCAG 2.2 additions are checked explicitly, since older tools and habits miss them:
- A11Y-12: Every accessibility bug gets a regression test at the lowest layer that can catch it (TEST-ARCH-11).
- A11Y-28: The UI stays usable in forced-colors mode (Windows contrast themes):
- A11Y-29: Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended (WCAG 2.2.1).
- A11Y-30: Submissions with legal or financial effect, or that change or delete user data, are reversible, checked, or confirmed (WCAG 3.3.4):
- A11Y-31: Content shown on hover or focus is dismissible, hoverable and persistent (WCAG 1.4.13):
- A11Y-32: Every page states its language in `<html lang>` (WCAG 3.1.1), also in a single-language product, and passages in another language carry their own `lang` (3.1.2).
- A11Y-33: Every chart has an accessible name and an equivalent in text with the same figures (WCAG 1.1.1, 1.3.1).
- A11Y-34: A read-only value within a known range (usage, quota, rating) is `role="meter"`; progress towards completion is `progressbar`.
- A11Y-13: Content reflows at 320 CSS px width without two-dimensional scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10).
- A11Y-14: Text-spacing overrides cause no clipped or overlapping text (WCAG 1.4.12):
- A11Y-15: No orientation lock (WCAG 1.3.4).
- A11Y-16: Target size (A11Y-10) is asserted on compact screens at L4, not only in the design system.
- A11Y-17: L4 runs in every viewport project, not only at desktop size.
- A11Y-18: The L6 checklist includes real 400 % browser zoom and text-only zoom (L6 release checklist).
- A11Y-19: Each project states its screen reader support matrix in its `docs/accessibility.md`.
- A11Y-20: Every status message is exposed without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3):
- A11Y-21: Every route has a unique, descriptive title (2.4.2), and focus moves to the new page's main heading when the path changes:
- A11Y-22: Input errors are identified in text and linked to the field programmatically.
- A11Y-23: Each main screen has a landmark and heading contract:
- A11Y-36: A control never changes the context while the user operates it (WCAG 3.2.2).
- A11Y-35: A wrapper never repeats the accessible name of the group, region or landmark it contains.
- A11Y-24: The screen reader protocol of the L6 release checklist runs once per release for every pair in the A11Y-19 matrix (tier T3, TS-TEST-18).
- A11Y-25: Real screen reader automation is optional and supplementary:

## [Taking Shortcuts Consciously](../11-risks-and-technical-debt/conscious-shortcuts.md)

- ARCH-SC-01: Projects start clean.
- ARCH-SC-02: Every shortcut taken on purpose is recorded as an Architecture Decision Record (ADR), stating context, decision, consequences and the trigger that should make us remove it.
- ARCH-SC-03 (default D6): ADRs live in `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md` in the consuming project, in Michael Nygard's format (Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences).
- ARCH-SC-04: The team agrees on explicit criteria for when a CRUD use case has "grown up".
- ARCH-SC-05: Some use cases stay CRUD forever.
- ARCH-SC-06: Agents MUST NOT introduce a shortcut silently.
- ARCH-SC-07: Incoming ports are required (default D1).
- ARCH-SC-08: An ADR or exception counts as an accepted deviation only for the rule IDs it names.
